chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, he said: Ibrahim ibn Raja' al-Jahdari narrated to me, he said: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us from Sharik ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
Whoever prefers anyone from my companions over Ali has indeed disbelieved.

key_terms.أصحابي: My companions, referring to the companions of the Prophet
key_terms.فضل: To prefer, to consider superior, to give precedence over
key_terms.كفر: Disbelief, denial of a fundamental truth of faith

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about preferring others over Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through a chain going back to the prominent companion Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) emphatically declared that placing any companion above Ali (AS) constitutes an act of disbelief. This hadith was transmitted in the scholarly assembly of Shaykh al-Saduq in 368 AH and reflects the deep-rooted Shia belief in the absolute superiority (afdaliyyah) of Imam Ali over all other companions, rooted in Quranic verses and numerous prophetic traditions.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim. He said: Ibrahim b. Raja’ al-Jahdari narrated to me. He said: Waki` b. al-Jarrah narrated to us from Sharik b. `Abdullah from `Abdullah b. Muhammad b. `Aqil from Jabir b. `Abdullah al-Ansari. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
He who prefers one of my companions over `Ali has disbelieved.
